name: Kestrel
description: A single-file H5 current account. The balance here is not a number but a line: today is the 17th, eight scheduled payments have still to leave before the month is out, and the app projects the balance forward over every one of them. Pausing a standing order, moving its payment day, or pulling money back out of a savings pot all bend that same line, and the forecast says exactly where its lowest point falls. As seeded it dips to -£72.49 on the 27th, one day before payday, and several different edits fix it. 11 screens, 15 transactions, 9 scheduled payments, 3 pots and a set of card controls.

finish.answer: final answer for question tasks; optional for action tasks

observation.text: engine.a11y(state) — the balance, the lowest projected point and the day-by-day forecast all serialise, so a text-only agent can reason about the line without seeing the chart.
observation.pixels: 390x844 screenshot (browser backend); __ENV__.bounds() maps every test-id to a pixel box
observation.state: engine.snapshot(state) — canonical state plus a derived view with every amount in pence. For the verifier only.

world.today: the 17th of March, fixed — a forecast reads the same however long an agent takes to reach it
world.money: integers in pence; the projection is a running sum, so the lowest point is exact
world.forecast: balance after each still-to-come scheduled payment, in day order
world.pause_vs_cancel: pausing skips this month, cancelling stops it for good; the forecast treats both the same way for the rest of the month
world.pots: money in a pot has left the current account, so it does not hold the forecast up until you move it back
